content.comment_body: Hello, what is the recommended method for transferring a value from a network output in [product_name] 1 to the network input in [product_name] 2? Currently, these [product_name] projects are not part of a network project. Is it possible to connect them using diagram mode, and if so, what approach should be used?

You can establish a connection between two [product_name] devices both in Diagram Mode and Network Project Mode. Using Network Project Mode with drag and drop is simplest, but I prefer configuring the connection manually in Network Project Mode. Alternatively, in Diagram Mode, you can set the first [product_name] as a client and the second as a server; after this setup, you can then import both diagrams into Network Project Mode to form a network project.

I was asking specifically about how to make network inputs and outputs function without using a network project. Should the I in the network output and the Q in the network input be used, or does it require configuring markers or variables instead? Is there any documentation or manual on setting up network inputs and outputs, as I haven't been able to locate one.
There is no single best method; use whatever works best for your scenario.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for effective ways to transfer network inputs and outputs between two [product_name] modules using Diagram Mode, outside of Network Project Mode. There is confusion due to limited documentation about handling network I/O, such as whether to use inputs (I), outputs (Q), markers (M), or variables (V). Because clear instructional resources are missing, users often have to rely on trial-and-error or community recommendations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear, straightforward instructions and documentation explaining how to set up network communication between devices within Diagram Mode, particularly concerning network I/O setup.
